*Fa-inna al-jannah hiya al-ma'wā* (then indeed Paradise will be the refuge): that is, the abode to which he returns after the reckoning.

*'An al-sā'ah* (about the Hour): that is, the Resurrection for reckoning and recompense.

*Ayyāna mursāhā* (when will be its appointed time): that is, when its occurrence and establishment will be.

*Fīma anta min dhikrāhā* (what are you of its mention): that is, you do not have knowledge of it so that you could mention it.

*Ilā Rabbika muntahāhā* (to your Lord is its finality): that is, the ultimate knowledge of it belongs to Allah alone, and no one else knows it.

*Lam yalbathū* (they did not remain): that is, in their graves.

*Illā 'ashiyyatan aw ḍuḥāhā* (except an evening or its morning): that is, an evening of a day, or the morning of that evening.

**Meaning of the verses:**

After Allah Most High explained the manifestations of His power in people's lives and what He created for them therein, as evidence for resurrection (*al-ba'th*) and recompense (*al-jaza'*), He mentions in these verses the manifestations of His power in the Hereafter, as evidence of His ability to resurrect them after death, to reckon them, and to recompense them. So He said, may He be exalted, ﴿Then when the Great Calamity comes﴾, meaning the Resurrection, and it was called the Great Calamity because it overwhelms everything, and nothing is greater than it: not the wind of 'Ād, nor the cry of Thamūd, nor the quaking of the Day of the Cloud. ﴿The Day when man will remember what he strove for﴾, of good or evil, because he will be certain that he will be reckoned and recompensed for his deeds. ﴿And Hellfire will be brought forth﴾, meaning Allah will make it manifest, so it will be visible to whoever sees it, and nothing will hide it. After that, people are divided into believer and disbeliever, and the paths are two: a path to Paradise and a path to the Fire. ﴿As for him who transgressed﴾, meaning he rebelled against the command of his Lord, disobeyed Him, and did not obey Him by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions. ﴿And preferred the worldly life﴾ over the Hereafter, so he worked for the world and devoted all his effort and capacity to it, and did not work for the Hereafter; he did not fast, nor pray, nor give charity, nor pay zakat. ﴿Then indeed Hellfire will be his refuge﴾, meaning it is his dwelling, his place of rest, and his abode; his drink is boiling water and his food is *zaqqūm*. ﴿But as for him who feared the standing before his Lord﴾, which is standing before Him to be questioned and recompensed, so he performed the obligations and avoided the prohibitions, ﴿and restrained the soul from desire﴾, meaning he restrained his own soul from its whims, so he did not respond to it in a desire that Allah hates, and did not obey it in anything Allah has forbidden. Then indeed Paradise, the abode of peace, and the righteous, the pious, and the good, is his refuge, and what an excellent refuge it is, where there are flowing springs, raised couches, placed cups, arranged cushions, spread carpets, and maidens with swelling breasts of equal age, and the meeting of loved ones. Allah Most High said: ﴿They ask you about the Hour: when will its appointing be?﴾, meaning they ask you, O our Messenger, those who deny resurrection, about the Hour, that is, its establishment, and when it will come to rest and be fixed. It is like a ship sailing night and day: when will it anchor? ﴿What are you of its mention?﴾, meaning you do not have knowledge of it so that you could mention it to them. ﴿To your Lord is its finality﴾: knowledge of the time of its coming and the hour of its anchoring belongs to Him alone, in order to transport people from their worldly life to their Hereafter, and with that their journey ends and their settlement is established. And their night and day come to an end. Allah Most High said: ﴿You are only a warner to those who fear it﴾, meaning the knowledge of it is not with you, O our Messenger, and the final outcome of its matter is not yours; your mission is other than what is asked of you. It is only a warning to those who fear the Hour and dread its arrival, because they believe in it and in what will happen in it of bliss and Hellfire. As for those who do not believe in it, they do not fear it, and their question about it is a question of mockery. So do not pay attention to them or concern yourself with them, for on the day they see it, it will seem to them that they did not remain in this worldly life and their graves ﴿except for an evening or its morning﴾, meaning an evening of a day or the morning of that evening, because of the terrors of the standing and the horrors of punishment they will face.

**Guidance of the verses:**

1. Affirmation of the creed of resurrection and recompense by mentioning its circumstances and attributes.
2. On the Day of Resurrection, people are divided into a pious believer in Paradise and a disbeliever and wicked person in the Fire.
3. Explanation that Allah Most High alone possesses the knowledge of the Unseen and of the Hour.
4. Explanation that some of the hardships make others forgotten, for the punishment of the grave is trivial before the punishment of the Fire.
